title: CACE-Bench: A Synthetic Agentic Evaluation Benchmark for LLM Credit-Pipeline Agents
description:
Compliance-Aware Credit-agent Evaluation (CACE-Bench): a fully synthetic, reproducible benchmark and generator for evaluating LLM-agent credit pipelines, and the self-evolution of such pipelines, under auditability constraints. No real personal or production credit data is used.

Version 0.6.0 adds the regulatory-shift track (evolve.py): a supervisory re-interpretation at 70 percent of a stream of screening alerts, three families of re-interpretation (threshold, scope, structural) at three severities, a dual-loop engine that may change only the runtime harness, and an admission gate whose every decision is written to a hash-chained log before deployment. Ten arms per cell, including no gate, gate on pre-shift labels, oracle, manual update and compute-matched local-only; 10 seeds per cell. Over 90 runs the gated dual loop admitted 144 of 7449 candidate changes with 0 admissions that increased error on a held-out half of the retrospective pool; the same loops without the gate admitted 309 such changes and ended with a missed-flag rate above 10 percent in 49 of 90 runs. The proposer in this track is a seeded search over a stated edit space, not a language model.

The reference run (cace_bench.py, seed 0, N = 23,000, registry 2026-08-03) is unchanged and now reports the missed-flag rate beside the false-positive rate and is replicated on seeds 0-4: silent-decision rate 55.11 to 6.53 percent; compliance false-positive rate 22.51 to 4.96 percent; missed-flag rate 15.30 to 3.47 percent; hallucination 2.55 to 0.62 percent; provenance completeness 93.40 to 99.33 percent. The recovery arm is a documented parametric model.

Scope. All figures characterise reference components on a synthetic distribution and are illustrative of the method, not of production performance. Provider-coverage figures are working assumptions. Protected attributes are omitted, so fairness auditing is out of scope. Every number in the accompanying paper is generated from the result files in this archive.
